title: Declare SQLAlchemy asyncio runtime dependency
intent: Declare the SQLAlchemy asyncio capability already used by app.db.pg_pool so clean installs include greenlet after SQLAlchemy 2.1.0 stopped supplying it implicitly on common platforms.
behavior_change: Fresh API dependency installs add greenlet through SQLAlchemy's supported asyncio extra; database URLs, pooling behavior, session behavior, and application code remain unchanged.

diff_articulation.what_changed: Changed the existing SQLAlchemy declaration to sqlalchemy[asyncio] and added a focused test that imports greenlet and the three asyncio symbols used by the pool module.
diff_articulation.why: The API imports AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker, and create_async_engine. Fresh installs resolving SQLAlchemy 2.1.0 fail test collection because greenlet is no longer an implicit platform dependency; SQLAlchemy's error directs asyncio users to install the asyncio extra.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: The existing aiosqlite dependency is a database driver, not SQLAlchemy's greenlet-based asyncio adaptation runtime. Previous green CI resolved SQLAlchemy 2.0.x, which supplied greenlet implicitly on x86_64 and masked the incomplete declaration.
diff_articulation.what_did_not_change: No SQLAlchemy version pin, lockfile, asyncpg dependency, database configuration, pool implementation, route, schema, or production behavior changed.
diff_articulation.why_structural_extraction: The supported SQLAlchemy extra owns its runtime dependency and version compatibility; declaring greenlet directly would duplicate that upstream dependency contract.

commands_run: Clean Python 3.11 base install resolved sqlalchemy 2.1.0 without greenlet and reproduced the test_pg_pool.py collection error
Clean Python 3.11 patched install resolved sqlalchemy 2.1.0 with greenlet 3.5.6
proofs: The pre-patch clean install reproduces the same missing-greenlet failure seen in Core CI.
The dependency delta is exactly greenlet; SQLAlchemy remains at 2.1.0 and no unrelated package moves.
The optional asyncpg test remains skipped when asyncpg is not installed.
verification.hardware: No hardware or manufacturing output involved.

files.intent: Declare SQLAlchemy's supported asyncio extra for the asyncio API already in use.
Prevent dependency declarations from again omitting the runtime required by the imported SQLAlchemy asyncio API.

findings: LOW: the unpinned SQLAlchemy declaration allowed an upstream minor release to expose a previously implicit runtime dependency. This patch declares the capability but deliberately does not introduce broader dependency pinning.
architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: The capability extra is the narrow upstream-supported repair. Version pinning or lockfile policy remains a separate dependency-governance decision.
